step/ask: You have a model, and you want a better one, with a lower loss. Before you train it, you would like to know the price: how much more compute will it take?
step/line: The runs of one family of models fall on a straight line on log-log axes, with a slope of minus alpha. Here alpha is zero point one.
step/step: Take one step to the right: ten times the compute. The line drops by alpha, so log L goes down by zero point one.
step/factor: Minus zero point one is the log of ten to the minus zero point one, and adding logs multiplies the numbers. So the loss is multiplied by ten to the minus zero point one: about zero point seven nine.
step/value: So a loss of three point nine eight, multiplied by that, becomes about three point one six.
step/same: Every step along a straight line has the same shape: across one power of ten, and down alpha. So every tenfold step multiplies the loss by the same factor, ten to the minus alpha.
step/law: The power law says so too. In L equals A times C to the minus alpha, replace C with ten times C, and the ten comes out as a factor of its own: ten to the minus alpha, times the old loss.
step/two: A hundred times the compute is two steps, so two factors. Multiplying adds the powers: ten to the minus zero point one, twice, is ten to the minus zero point two, about zero point six three.
step/k: So k steps of ten multiply the loss by ten to the minus k alpha. Three steps, a thousand times the compute, give ten to the minus zero point three: about a half.
shrink/plain: Now put the loss axis back to plain numbers, and keep the tenfold steps across.
shrink/drops: The steps no longer match. Each takes the same fraction off a smaller loss, so the drops shrink: zero point eight two, then zero point six five, then zero point five one.
shrink/price: And each step costs ten times the compute of the one before. The last step here takes off the least, and its run costs a hundred times the first one's.
shrink/kaplan: Measured exponents are smaller still. In 2020, Jared Kaplan and colleagues measured alpha at about zero point zero five, for language models given more and more compute.
shrink/tenth: Then each tenfold step multiplies the loss by ten to the minus zero point zero five: only about zero point eight nine.
shrink/million: Halving the loss takes six such steps, since six times zero point zero five is zero point three. Six steps of ten: a million times the compute.
back/given: Now a different family. One run ends at a loss of four, and a run with ten times its compute ends at three point two. What loss will a hundred times the compute reach?
back/factor: First find the factor per step: three point two over four is zero point eight.
back/again: A hundred times the compute is one more tenfold step past three point two, so multiply by zero point eight again: two point five six.
back/not: Not three point two minus another zero point eight, which would give two point four. The factor stays the same, so the drops shrink.
back/back: Now run it backwards. A loss of four should become two point five six: how much more compute does that take? Divide first: two point five six over four is zero point six four.
back/count: Zero point six four is zero point eight times zero point eight: two factors, so two tenfold steps.
back/hundred: Each step is ten times the compute, so two steps cost ten times ten: a hundred times the compute.
